questions.sec: Mechanism of Action Ladder and Drug-Action Table
questions.q: Step 1: MHC presents foreign antigens to local immune cells. Which drug blocks production of inflammatory mediators by these local immune cells?
questions.exp: Steroids block production of inflammatory mediators by local immune cells (Book p272)

questions.sec: Mechanism of Action Ladder and Drug-Action Table
questions.q: Activated calcineurin removes PO4 from ____ (NFATc-PO4 → NFATc).
questions.exp: Calcineurin dephosphorylates NFATc-PO4 → NFATc (Book p272)

questions.sec: Mechanism of Action Ladder and Drug-Action Table
questions.q: NFATc + NFATn in the nucleus ↑ transcription factor for ____ synthesis.
questions.exp: ↑ transcription factor for IL-2 (Book p272)

questions.sec: Mechanism of Action Ladder and Drug-Action Table
questions.q: Match the immunomodulator pair to its action.
questions.exp: Cyclosporin/tacrolimus → calcineurin; basiliximab/daclizumab → IL-2R CD25; everolimus/sirolimus → mTOR; azathioprine/methotrexate → S-phase (Book p272)

questions.sec: Mechanism of Action Ladder and Drug-Action Table
questions.q: Match the agent acting on activated lymphocytes to its target.
questions.exp: Muromonab → CD3; alemtuzumab → CD52; steroids induce apoptosis of activated lymphocytes (Book p272)

questions.sec: Mechanism of Action Ladder and Drug-Action Table
questions.q: The IL-2 receptor on the CD-8 cell is also called ____.
questions.exp: IL-2 receptor/CD-25 (Book p272)

questions.sec: Mechanism of Action Ladder and Drug-Action Table
questions.q: Match the transplant scenario to the drug policy.
questions.exp: GVHD treatment & prophylaxis and rejection prophylaxis: all drugs; rejection treatment: drugs acting on activated lymphocytes (Book p272)

questions.sec: Mechanism of Action Ladder and Drug-Action Table
questions.q: Treatment of graft rejection specifically uses:
questions.exp: Graft rejection treatment: drugs acting on activated lymphocytes (Book p272)

questions.q: Calcineurin inhibitors work by ↓ ____ synthesis.
questions.exp: MOA: ↓ IL-2 synthesis (Book p273)

questions.q: First line for GVHD/graft rejection is cyclosporine (less effective, less toxic). The second-line 'rescue drug' (more effective, more toxic) is:
questions.exp: No response → second line tacrolimus (rescue drug: more effective, more toxic) (Book p273)

questions.q: For skin disorders (lichen planus, atopic dermatitis), steroid-resistant ulcerative colitis & nephrotic syndrome, myasthenia gravis, RA and Behcet's disease, the DOC is ____.
questions.exp: DOC: cyclosporine (Book p273)

questions.q: Match the calcineurin-inhibitor S/E pattern to its list.
right: Hirsutism, hyperplasia of gums, hyperlipidemia, hyperuricemia
questions.exp: Both: neuro/nephro/hepatotoxicity, hyperkalemia, hyperglycemia; cyclosporine adds hirsutism, gum hyperplasia, hyperlipidemia, hyperuricemia; S/E tacrolimus > cyclosporine (Book p273)

questions.q: Side effects overall are greater with ____ than with cyclosporine.
questions.exp: Tacrolimus > cyclosporine (Book p273)

questions.q: Cyclosporine-specific S/E: hirsutism and ____ of gums.
questions.exp: Hyperplasia of gums (Book p273)

questions.q: mTOR inhibitors block the ____ phase of cell proliferation.
questions.exp: Blocks G1–S phase of cell proliferation (Book p273)

questions.q: Sirolimus (rapamycin) is used for:
opts: GVHD & graft rejection add-on, cardiac stent coating, uvoretinitis
Renal cell cancer, angiomyolipoma, pancreatic cancer, astrocytoma
Rheumatoid arthritis, CAPS, JIA and Still's disease
Multiple sclerosis and acute graft rejection prophylaxis
questions.exp: Sirolimus: GVHD, graft rejection add-on, cardiac stent coating, uvoretinitis (Book p273)

questions.q: Temsirolimus is used for ____ cancer.
questions.exp: Temsirolimus: renal cell cancer (Book p273)

questions.q: Everolimus covers which cancer set?
opts: Renal cell cancer, renal angiomyolipoma, pancreatic cancer, ER(+) breast cancer, astrocytoma
CML, pancreatic cancer, malignant melanoma, sarcoidosis, Behcet's disease
Renal cell cancer, cardiac stent coating, uvoretinitis, GVHD add-on
CAPS, Still's disease, acute gout, RA and multiple sclerosis
questions.exp: Everolimus: renal cell cancer, renal angiomyolipoma, pancreatic cancer, ER(+) breast cancer, astrocytoma (Book p273)

questions.q: In 'Lymphocytes hate mTOR', the raised-lipid item is ____ (hyperlipidemia).
questions.exp: Lymphocele, HUS, myelosuppression, thrombocytopenia, oral ulcers, raised lipids (Book p274)

questions.q: Match the antibody to its MOA/use.
right: IL-2R/CD25 inhibitor → prophylaxis of acute graft rejection
CD3 inhibitor → Rx of acute graft rejection
CD52 inhibitor → graft rejection & multiple sclerosis
questions.exp: Daclizumab → MS; basiliximab → acute rejection prophylaxis; muromonab → Rx acute rejection; alemtuzumab → rejection & MS (Book p274)

questions.q: Muromonab's S/E is ____ syndrome, C/I with fever + chills.
questions.exp: Cytokine release syndrome (C/I: fever + chills) (Book p274)

questions.q: Match the T-cell-activation blocker to its target.
right: Blocks CD80/86 → inhibits T cell activation
Blocks CD3 → inhibits T cell activation
questions.exp: Abatacept/belatacept → CD80/86; alefacept → CD3; azathioprine → S-phase (Book p274)

questions.q: Belatacept is used for prophylaxis of graft rejection in ____ transplant.
questions.exp: Prophylaxis of graft rejection in renal transplant (Book p274)

questions.q: Alefacept gives prophylaxis of ____ graft rejection.
questions.exp: Prophylaxis of drug-resistant graft rejection (Book p274)

questions.q: Azathioprine is a prodrug of ____.
questions.exp: Prodrug of 6-mercaptopurine (Book p274)

questions.q: Azathioprine/6-MP are metabolized by ____ (TPMT); deficiency ↑ risk of toxicity.
questions.exp: Metabolized by thiopurine methyltransferase (TPMT) → ↑ toxicity if enzyme deficient (Book p275)

questions.q: Mycophenolate mofetil is selectively lymphotoxic because it:
opts: Inhibits IMP dehydrogenase → blocks de-novo purine synthesis, the lymphocyte's only purine pathway
Blocks salvage purine synthesis equally in all dividing cells
Inhibits pyrimidine de-novo synthesis, hitting all immune cells alike
Blocks IL-2 receptor CD25, silencing T-cell proliferation signals
questions.exp: Inhibits IMP dehydrogenase → de-novo purine synthesis (only pathway in lymphocytes) → selective toxicity (Book p274)

questions.q: Mycophenolate mofetil is ____ with azathioprine.
questions.exp: C/I with azathioprine (Book p274)

questions.q: In transplant, mycophenolate is:
opts: First-line in cardiac/bone marrow transplant; 2nd line in other transplants
2nd line in cardiac transplant; first-line elsewhere
questions.exp: Cardiac/bone marrow transplant: first-line; other transplant: 2nd line (Book p274)

questions.q: Match the IL-1 inhibitor to its use.
right: RA; DOC in CAPS; Rx of JIA/Still's disease
questions.exp: Anakinra → RA, DOC CAPS, JIA/Still's; canakinumab → CAPS, Still's; rilonacept → acute gout (Book p274)

questions.q: CAPS = ____ associated periodic syndrome (anakinra is DOC).
questions.exp: Cryopyrin associated periodic syndrome (Book p274)

questions.q: For T-cell activation, T-cell CD28 binds APC ____ while CD2 binds LFA-3.
questions.exp: CD28–CD80/86 and CD2–LFA-3 drive T-cell activation (Book p275)

questions.q: Thalidomide was introduced as a ____ and banned for morning sickness due to phocomelia.
questions.exp: Introduced as sedative/hypnotic; banned d/t phocomelia in newborn (Book p275)

questions.q: Thalidomide was reintroduced for all of the following effects EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Reintroduced d/t anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, anti-neoplastic, anti-angiogenic effects (Book p275)

questions.q: The 'Catch PROGRAMMES' uses of thalidomide include all EXCEPT:
opts: Behcet's disease and AIDS-related aphthous ulcer
questions.exp: Uses: CML, pancreatic cancer, RA, oro-ocular genital syndrome (Behcet's), GVHD/graft rejection, AIDS aphthous ulcer, multiple myeloma, malignant melanoma, erythema nodosum leprosum, sarcoidosis (Book p275)

questions.q: In the 'SPORT Channel' S/E mnemonic, the final C stands for ____.
questions.exp: Sedation, peripheral neuropathy, phocomelia, ocular S/E, rash, thrombosis, constipation (Book p275)

questions.q: Oro-ocular genital syndrome treated by thalidomide is ____ disease.
questions.exp: Oro-ocular genital syndrome (Behcet's disease) (Book p275)

units.title: Mechanism of Action Ladder and Drug-Action Table
units.sec: Mechanism of Action Ladder and Drug-Action Table · p272
units.guide: MHC presents antigen → calcineurin (steroids block mediators) → NFATc dephosphorylation → NFATc+NFATn → ↑IL-2 transcription. IL-2R = CD25 (basiliximab/daclizumab). mTOR (everolimus/sirolimus) G1→S; azathioprine/methotrexate S-phase. Muromonab CD3; alemtuzumab CD52; steroids apoptosis. GVHD & rejection prophylaxis: all drugs; rejection treatment: drugs on activated lymphocytes.

units.title: Calcineurin Inhibitors
units.guide: ↓IL-2 synthesis. First line cyclosporine (less effective/less toxic); rescue tacrolimus (more effective/more toxic). DOC cyclosporine for skin disorders, steroid-resistant UC/nephrotic, MG, RA, Behcet's. S/E both: neuro/nephro/hepatotoxicity, hyperkalemia, hyperglycemia; cyclosporine adds hirsutism, gum hyperplasia, hyperlipidemia, hyperuricemia; tacrolimus > cyclosporine.

units.title: mTOR Inhibitors
units.guide: Block G1–S. Sirolimus (rapamycin): GVHD/rejection add-on, cardiac stent coating, uvoretinitis. Temsirolimus: renal cell cancer. Everolimus: renal cell cancer, angiomyolipoma, pancreatic, ER(+) breast, astrocytoma. S/E 'Lymphocytes hate mTOR': lymphocele, HUS, myelosuppression, thrombocytopenia, oral ulcers, raised lipids.

units.title: Other Immunomodulators: Antibodies
units.guide: Daclizumab → MS; basiliximab → acute rejection prophylaxis (both IL-2R/CD25). Muromonab CD3 → Rx acute rejection, cytokine release syndrome (C/I fever+chills). Alemtuzumab CD52. Abatacept/belatacept CD80/86 (belatacept renal transplant); alefacept CD3 → drug-resistant rejection.

units.title: Azathioprine, Mycophenolate and IL-1 Inhibitors
units.sec: Azathioprine, Mycophenolate and IL-1 Inhibitors · p274
units.guide: Azathioprine = prodrug of 6-MP; TPMT deficiency ↑ toxicity; blocks S-phase. MMF inhibits IMP dehydrogenase (de-novo purines, lymphocyte-only pathway); C/I with azathioprine; 1st line cardiac/bone-marrow, 2nd line others. IL-1 inhibitors: anakinra (RA, DOC CAPS, JIA/Still's), canakinumab (CAPS, Still's), rilonacept (acute gout).

units.title: Thalidomide
units.guide: CD28–CD80/86, CD2–LFA-3 = T-cell activation. Thalidomide: sedative/hypnotic → banned (phocomelia) → reintroduced (anti-inflammatory/immunomodulatory/anti-neoplastic/anti-angiogenic). Uses Catch PROGRAMMES; S/E SPORT Channel (sedation, peripheral neuropathy, phocomelia, ocular, rash, thrombosis, constipation).
